title: Intent liberator: install from Homebrew, hands off rhadamanth
objective: Molt's intent liberator installs and checks Intent the way an everyday user gets it, from Homebrew, and its verdict names the Intent that `intent` actually runs. Molt stops managing Intent on rhadamanth, the machine Intent is developed on.
context:
On 23 Sep 2026 gyges's `molt upgrade` warned that PATH resolves `intent` to `/opt/homebrew/bin/intent`, not `~/bin/intent`, and still printed `intent: ✓ ok`. Measured on gyges the same morning: the link Molt managed pointed at Intent 2.6.0 (the v2 script in a frozen, pre-rewrite checkout), login shells ran Homebrew's 3.2.0, and an interactive non-login shell ran 2.6.0. The check never asked which version it had linked, and its shadow warning went quiet in exactly the shell where v2 ran. v2.6.0 refuses a v3 project with an error and writes nothing, so nothing was damaged.

hv's rulings the same day: gyges is the test bed for running Intent from brew like an everyday user, with no local copy of the dev tree, and problems with that go to intent-vc. Nothing to do with Intent on rhadamanth may be touched. Do just enough to prove it works.

The liberator's source-checkout mode had two intended users. rhadamanth is now off limits, and kovacs has no Intent and does not list the liberator. So the liberator becomes brew-only rather than keep a mode that no machine runs.

wps.title: Keep Molt off Intent on rhadamanth
Retire gyges's Intent v2 links and checkout (hv's action)

criteria.text: On gyges, molt upgrade reports the intent liberator ok, naming the Homebrew Intent that a login shell runs.

state.evidence: gyges-infra, 2026-09-23: molt upgrade exit 0 at Molt 70504ca / Molt-matts 857d49c -- 'Zen: intent: Homebrew's intent 3.2.0 (4e2f908a5857c4ac878aa8f071c5f09b60753993) runs from PATH and the gate' then 'intent: ✓ ok'; no warning or error lines

criteria.text: The intent check fails, naming the path, when intent on PATH is not Homebrew's.
The intent check fails when the gate home names an install directory that no longer exists.
Molt does nothing with Intent on rhadamanth: the intent liberator is disabled in its manifest and no Intent file there was changed.

state.evidence: Molt-matts 857d49c: rhadamanth manifest intent enabled=false; 'molt list' on rhadamanth prints 'intent: disabled'. Only read-only probes of rhadamanth's Intent (one git status there before hv's ruling can refresh the index stat cache).

criteria.text: gyges has no Intent v2 links and no local Intent checkout.

state.evidence: gyges-infra, 2026-09-23, with hv's approval: ~/bin/intent, ~/.local/bin/intent and ~/Devel/prj/Intent all 'No such file or directory'; login and non-login zsh resolve /opt/homebrew/bin/intent, intent 3.2.0 (4e2f908a5)

tests.note: @test 'intent_check FAILS, naming it, when PATH runs another intent'. Not observed red: written with the rewrite, and the pre-ST0004 liberator had no brew path to fail. Green at 70504ca under bash 5.3 and /bin/bash 3.2.

@test 'intent_check FAILS when the gate home names an install that is gone'. Not observed red: written with the rewrite, and the pre-ST0004 liberator had no brew path to fail. Green at 70504ca under bash 5.3 and /bin/bash 3.2.
